entries.subject: Proudfoot et al. (2026) occultation and satellite-orbit Maclaurin model
entries.finding: The selected shape is the published smooth Maclaurin model with semiaxes 329, 329 and 294 km, combining an occultation silhouette with the satellite orbit; the source survey was checked on 2026-09-09.

entries.subject: J2000 pole prior from satellite-orbit alignment
entries.finding: The display uses the published J2000 pole prior at right ascension 20.6 +/-1.5 degrees and declination 46.25 +/-0.32 degrees, taken from satellite-orbit alignment, with an arbitrary reference meridian.

entries.subject: Slightly triaxial fit permitted by the same observations
entries.finding: The README records that the adopted model assumes an equatorial satellite orbit and that the source also permits a slightly triaxial fit, so the satellite-orbit alignment and the competing triaxial interpretation remain unresolved.
entries.revisitWhen: An independent pole determination or a new occultation campaign decides between the Maclaurin and triaxial fits.

entries.subject: 11.05-hour photometric period
entries.finding: The photometric period has aliases, so it is not installed as a qualified sidereal spin and no absolute surface attitude is claimed.
entries.revisitWhen: An alias-free rotation period or an absolute surface-attitude determination is published.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No reconstructed surface texture is supplied and the smooth model resolves no terrain, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid with Shadows off by default.

entries.subject: Surface spectra and unresolved observations as surface textures
entries.finding: The source survey records that surface spectra and unresolved observations are not reconstructed surface textures, so none is used for the displayed surface.
entries.revisitWhen: A resolved surface map or reconstructed texture for this body is released.
